chapters.title: Chapter 2: Who Needs to Pay Advance Tax

lessons.title: Senior Citizens and Other Taxpayers Who Are Exempt

body.text: One group of taxpayers is excused from advance tax altogether: resident individuals aged 60 or over who have no income from business or profession. They still owe the tax. They simply pay it once, before filing their return, instead of in four instalments. Add even a small consulting practice or a trading account, and the exemption disappears.

children.text: Retirement changes how income arrives. The monthly salary with TDS gives way to pension, FD interest, dividends and the occasional mutual fund redemption, much of it with little or no tax deducted. Asking a 70-year-old to estimate all of that four times a year would be a heavy burden, so the law makes an exception. This lesson shows exactly who qualifies, who does not, and what the exemption does and does not protect you from.

markDefs.definition: An individual who is resident in India for the tax year and is 60 years of age or older at any time during that tax year.
The head of income covering business, trading, freelancing and professional practice, including F&O and intraday trading, consulting and any income declared under the presumptive schemes.

body.title: Quick Check: Does the Exemption Apply?
body.question: Which of these resident taxpayers is exempt from paying advance tax for tax year 2026-27?
options: Mrs Das, 72, Kolkata, whose only income apart from pension is profit from trading Nifty options
Mr Shetty, who turns 60 in November 2026, with income only from pension, FD interest and mutual fund redemptions
Mr Bose, 58, who took voluntary retirement and now lives on FD interest and rent
Mrs Menon, 67, a retired professor who earns fees for guest lectures and paper evaluation as an independent consultant
body.explanation: Mr Shetty turns 60 during the tax year, is resident and has no business or professional income, so he is exempt for the whole of tax year 2026-27. Mrs Das has F&O income, which is business income. Mr Bose is under 60. Mrs Menon earns professional fees as a consultant. Each of them must pay advance tax if their tax after TDS is ₹10,000 or more.

children.text: His slab income is above ₹12 lakh, so no rebate applies, and marginal relief does not help because ₹78,750 is less than the ₹1,25,000 by which he crosses ₹12 lakh. Under the new regime, senior citizens use the same slabs as everyone else.

body.label: Mr Raghavan's tax still due after TDS
body.context: Well above ₹10,000. A 55-year-old in the same position would owe it as advance tax in four instalments. Because he is a resident senior citizen with no business income, he pays it once, before filing his return, with no interest for skipping instalments.

body.title: Try It: If the Gain Were Smaller
body.prompt: Suppose Mr Raghavan's long-term gain was ₹2,25,000 instead of ₹5,00,000, with everything else unchanged. How much self-assessment tax would he pay before filing? Include 4% cess and answer in rupees.
body.explanation: Slab tax stays ₹78,750. Tax on the gain becomes 12.5% of ₹1,00,000 (after the ₹1,25,000 exemption), which is ₹12,500. Total before cess is ₹91,250, and with 4% cess ₹94,900. Subtracting ₹80,000 of TDS leaves ₹14,900. Still no advance tax, because the exemption does not depend on the amount.

body.text: The exemption removes the obligation to pay in instalments, so the interest for not paying advance tax and for missed instalments does not arise. It does not remove the deadline for filing. If a senior citizen pays the balance and files the return late, interest for late filing under section 423 (old 234A) still applies on the unpaid tax. Pay the self-assessment tax and file on time.

children.text: When a Senior Citizen Loses the Exemption

columns.label: Retired on pension and investments
points: Income: pension, FD interest, rent, dividends, capital gains
Exempt from advance tax, whatever the amount
Pays any balance as self-assessment tax before filing

columns.label: Retired but still earning from work or trading
points: Income includes consulting, tutoring, a shop, freelancing, F&O or intraday
Business or professional income of any size
Loses the exemption for the entire tax year
Advance tax applies to the total tax, not just the tax on business income

children.text: Mrs Kulkarni is 63, a retired chartered engineer in Pune who now consults for small manufacturers. Her clients are individuals and proprietors who deduct no TDS. Her receipts of ₹30,00,000 qualify for the presumptive scheme for professionals, so her professional income is ₹15,00,000. With pension of ₹4,00,000, her total income is ₹18,25,000 and her tax is ₹1,71,600. Her age does not help: she has professional income, so she must pay advance tax, though as a presumptive taxpayer she can pay all of it by 15 March 2027.

body.title: Scenario: Mr Iqbal Starts a Coaching Class
body.scenario: Mr Iqbal, 66, is a retired bank officer in Lucknow on the new regime. His pension is ₹7,00,000 and he earns ₹6,00,000 of FD interest from one bank, which deducts 10% TDS. In April 2026 he starts coaching students for banking exams from home, and keeps simple books. His profit from coaching for tax year 2026-27 is ₹4,50,000. His son tells him not to worry about advance tax because "senior citizens are exempt".
body.prompt: Is his son right? Work out whether Mr Iqbal owes advance tax, how much, and what he should have paid by each due date. How would his position differ without the coaching income?
body.modelAnswer: His son is wrong. Coaching income is business or professional income, so Mr Iqbal loses the senior citizen exemption for the whole of tax year 2026-27. His total income is ₹16,75,000: pension after the ₹75,000 standard deduction (₹6,25,000), FD interest (₹6,00,000) and coaching profit (₹4,50,000). Slab tax is ₹20,000 plus ₹40,000 plus ₹60,000 plus 20% of ₹75,000 (₹15,000), which is ₹1,35,000, or ₹1,40,400 with cess. TDS is ₹60,000 on the FD interest, and nil on pension because tax on pension alone is rebated. That leaves ₹80,400, which is well above ₹10,000. Since he keeps regular books rather than using a presumptive scheme, the normal schedule applies: cumulative ₹12,060 by 15 June, ₹36,180 by 15 September, ₹60,300 by 15 December and ₹80,400 by 15 March. Without the coaching income, his income would be ₹12,25,000, his tax just ₹26,000 after marginal relief, less than the ₹60,000 of TDS, and he would be exempt from advance tax and due a refund. A ₹4,50,000 side business changed not just his tax, but his whole payment schedule.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Age Test
body.textWithBlank: To qualify for the advance tax exemption, a resident individual must be ___ years of age or older at any time during the tax year and have no business or professional income.
body.explanation: The age is 60, and it only has to be reached at some point during the tax year. There is no separate advance tax rule for super senior citizens aged 80 or more: they are covered by the same exemption on the same conditions.

children.text: Everyone Else Who Pays No Advance Tax
The senior citizen exemption is the only true category exemption. Everyone else who pays no advance tax is simply below the line, or has it covered another way.

body.text: Non-resident Indians get no age-based exemption. An NRI aged 65 who owns a let-out flat in Bengaluru is liable for advance tax in principle. In practice, tenants and buyers deducting TDS on payments to non-residents, often at high rates, usually cover most or all of the tax, which is why many NRIs never pay an instalment.

body.title: Senior Citizen Advance Tax Review
steps: Confirm residential status for the tax year, especially if they spent long periods abroad
Confirm they are 60 or older at some point between 1 April and 31 March
List every income source and flag anything that is business or professional: consulting, tutoring, rent from a commercial activity run as a business, F&O or intraday trades
If none are flagged, skip the instalments, but estimate tax and plan to pay the balance as self-assessment tax before filing
If any are flagged, treat them like any other taxpayer: run the ₹10,000 test and follow the instalment schedule
Download AIS early in the new tax year to catch interest and dividends from accounts they may have forgotten

body.label: Senior Citizens and Super Senior Citizens: Income Tax Department
body.description: The official guide to tax provisions for individuals aged 60 and above, including the advance tax exemption and return filing.

cards.definition: An individual resident in India who is 60 or older at any time during the tax year.
A resident senior citizen with no business or professional income need not pay advance tax. Old section 207(2).
Includes consulting, tutoring, shops, freelancing, presumptive income, F&O and intraday trading. Any amount removes the senior citizen exemption.
Exempt seniors pay any balance as self-assessment tax under minor head 300 before filing.
Interest under section 423 (old 234A) still applies if the return is filed late with tax unpaid, even for exempt seniors.
A resident aged 75 or more with only pension and interest from the same bank, who can have the bank deduct full tax and need not file a return. Old section 194P.

points: Resident individuals aged 60 or more at any time in the tax year, with no business or professional income, are exempt from advance tax
The exemption is from instalments, not from tax: any balance is paid as self-assessment tax before filing
Exempt seniors avoid interest for skipped instalments, but still pay interest if they file late with tax unpaid
Any business or professional income, including consulting, tutoring, F&O or intraday trading, removes the exemption for the entire tax year
Under the new regime, seniors use the same slabs as everyone else; there is no separate advance tax rule for those aged 80 or more
Non-residents have no age-based exemption, though TDS on their Indian income often covers most of the tax

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or investment advice. Section references are to the Income-tax Act, 2025, with corresponding Income-tax Act, 1961 sections where the new provision is referred to by its familiar old number. Examples use new regime rates for tax year 2026-27 as understood at the time of writing, which can change with each Union Budget. Residential status and the nature of income can be complex for retirees. Verify current rules or consult a qualified chartered accountant before acting.
